Academic Writing · Life Pre-Intermediate

Paragraph Writing Practice

Long-term & Pharmacy students · Terms 1–4 · 384 prompts4 timed steps · 55 minutesMarked and returned by your teacher

Before you start

Choose a prompt

Every prompt comes from a speaking topic of your module: the cue card or one of its Part 3 questions. Each topic gives all six paragraph types. Codes start with your group: DH = long-term students, DUOC = pharmacy students.

4 timed steps

  1. Topic sentence · 5′
  2. Outline · 15′
  3. Concluding sentence · 5′
  4. Full paragraph · 30′
  5. Submit

Theory recap

Write an academic paragraph in 4 steps

Topic sentence (5′) → Outline (15′) → Concluding sentence (5′) → Full paragraph (30′). Full lesson ↗

How your paragraph is marked

The teacher marks your paragraph with the paragraph rubric of Rubric chấm chữa Writing tổng hợp: 5 criteria, each 0–5. Mark /10 = total /25 × 0.4.

Task fulfilment & relevance

/5

  • Answers every part of the task
  • All content relevant to the topic
  • One clear focus
  • Academic register
Paragraph structure & development

/5

  • Topic sentence with a controlling idea
  • 2 main points: point 1 with an example, point 2 with a result
  • Every sentence supports the main idea
  • Concluding sentence, no new idea
Organisation, coherence & cohesion

/5

  • Logical order
  • A signal for each main point, used for the right function
  • Reference words and synonyms
  • No mechanical linking
Lexical resource

/5

  • Precise topic words and collocations
  • Signal language of the paragraph type
  • Little repetition
  • Correct spelling, no contractions
Grammatical range & accuracy

/5

  • Simple and complex sentences
  • Accurate grammar
  • Punctuation and capital letters
Rules applied before marking
  • Under 120 words: Task fulfilment at most 3 (up to 30% short) or 2 (more than 30% short)
  • 20 words or fewer: Task fulfilment 1, every other criterion at most 1
  • Partly off-topic: every criterion at most 3
  • Off-topic: Task fulfilment 1, marked OFF-TOPIC in the comment
  • Sentences copied from the task do not count

The 3-part paragraph · 120–200 words · 8–10 sentences

Topic sentence (TS)1 sentence
Topic + controlling idea: what the paragraph will prove.
Main point 1 + details3–4 sentences
The point → explain (why / how) → example (a case, a place, a figure).
Main point 2 + details3–4 sentences
Opens with Another… / In addition, → explain → result.
Concluding sentence (CS)1 sentence
Restate · sum up · final comment. No new idea.
5′Step 1 · Topic sentence
  • Read the task
  • Choose the controlling idea
  • Write 1 sentence
15′Step 2 · Outline
  • 2 main points
  • Explain each one
  • Example for point 1 · Result for point 2
5′Step 3 · Concluding sentence
  • Restate, sum up or comment
  • No new idea
30′Step 4 · Full paragraph
  • Follow the outline
  • Signal each point
  • Check unity and grammar

Step 1 Topic sentence = topic + controlling idea

Formula
Studying abroad = topic · helps young people become more independent = controlling idea
Too broad
Technology is important. → Online banking has made personal finance faster and safer.
Just a fact
Hanoi has about 8.5 million people. → Rapid population growth has put Hanoi's public transport under serious pressure.
Announcement
In this paragraph, I will talk about pets. → Keeping a pet can improve elderly people's mental health.
Two ideas
Cities offer good jobs, and the countryside has cleaner air. → Big cities offer young graduates a wider range of jobs.

Step 2 Outline: 2 main points, each explained and illustrated

TS
Studying abroad helps young people become more independent.
Main point 1
  • manage daily life alone
  • Explain cook, pay bills, solve problems without parents
  • Example a student in Australia learns to budget a monthly allowance
Main point 2
  • make decisions about study and career
  • Explain choose courses, look for part-time jobs
  • Result more confident when they start work

Notes, not sentences. Find details with who? what? when? where? why? how? · PEEL = Point · Explain · Example · Link.

Step 3 Concluding sentence: 3 ways to close

① Restate the TSSame idea, new words
In short, living overseas teaches young people to stand on their own feet.
② Sum up the pointsName both points
By managing money and making their own choices, students abroad become far more self-reliant.
③ Final commentJudgement, prediction, advice
For this reason, a period of study overseas can be a valuable investment.

Step 4 Write the paragraph from the plan

Open main point 1
First, · The main reason is that… · One benefit of … is that…
Open main point 2
In addition, · Another reason is that… · Moreover,
Explain
This means that… · In other words, · This is because…
Example
For example, · For instance, · A good example is…
Result
As a result, · Therefore, · Consequently,
Check
  • Unity: every sentence supports the controlling idea
  • Coherence: key words repeated, pronouns consistent, logical order
  • One paragraph, no contractions, verb forms, plurals, articles

The 6 paragraph types

A · Causes

There are two main reasons why young people leave rural areas.

becausedue toone reason isthis is caused by

B · Effects

Deforestation has serious effects on local communities.

as a resultthereforeleads toresults in

C · Advantages – disadvantages

Working from home offers employees several advantages.

one advantage isanother benefithoweveron the other hand

D · Problem – solution

Traffic congestion could be reduced by two practical measures.

one solution isshouldcouldby + V-ing

E · Compare – contrast

Online and face-to-face classes differ in two important ways.

similarlylikewisewhereasin contrast

F · Opinion

I believe that university education should be free.

I believein my viewfirstlyfor this reason

Settings

Class assignments

A student whose Class starts with a class code below (e.g. code Lớp A1) writes one of the prompts ticked for that class (one ticked = everyone writes it). Prompts are grouped by module (HP1–HP4) and paragraph type; each shows whether it is for long-term (dài hạn) or pharmacy (dược) students. The 4 steps are timed 5 + 15 + 5 + 30 minutes; the paragraph is submitted automatically at the end of Step 4. With no class listed, every student chooses freely.
Several classes can practise in the same week: add one row per class, each with its own prompts and deadline. Students see every open code and pick their own; after the deadline the page and the class records accept no more paragraphs for that code. Remove a row to close a class at once.

Teacher accounts

Teachers sign in with their name and password to review, mark and release paragraphs. Type an existing name to give that person a new password (your own name changes your password).
